caption:
Can I still have this while pregnant?
The honest answer is that almost nobody has studied it.

Not every no means the same thing. Some answers mean there is no data, because the category was never studied in pregnancy. Some mean there are case reports and nothing more. And some mean there is a known mechanism to avoid, which is a different and much stronger statement. "We do not know" and "we know it is harmful" are different sentences, and they are often delivered in the same tone.

A systematic review of the published literature on cosmetic procedures in pregnancy and lactation found no controlled trials. What it could draw on was case reports and small case series. That is not a finding that anything is unsafe. It is a finding that the evidence to say either way was not there - which is exactly why the answer you are given should name its own uncertainty.

So the useful questions are not about booking. What is this based on - trials, case reports, or habit. Can it wait, given that most of this is elective by definition. And who else should know, starting with the people managing the pregnancy.

Waiting is a plan. Usually it is the better one.

General education only.

first_comment: The sentence worth listening for is whether you are being told a no or an unknown - they sound the same and they are not. What question would you most want answered?
